bib.title: Align your Latents: High-Resolution Video Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

question: Can a pretrained image latent diffusion model be turned into a high-resolution video generator by training only inserted temporal layers?
hypothesis: Freezing pretrained spatial layers and training temporal alignment layers (plus a video-fine-tuned decoder and upsampler) gives temporally consistent high-resolution video efficiently.
contributions: Efficient approach for high-resolution, long-term consistent video generation by inserting temporal layers into pretrained image LDMs
State-of-the-art on real driving scene videos, multi-minute generation
Stable Diffusion turned into a text-to-video LDM
Learned temporal layers combine with other image checkpoints (DreamBooth)

method.summary: Image LDM is pretrained (or Stable Diffusion used), spatial layers frozen, temporal attention and 3D-conv residual layers interleaved with a learned alpha merge are trained on encoded video; decoder gets temporal layers and a video patch discriminator. Prediction (0/1/2 context frames) and interpolation (T to 4T, 4T to 16T) models plus a 4x video-aware upsampler form a cascade.

datasets.name: RDS (in-house real driving scenes)
datasets.size: 683,060 videos of 8 s at 512x1024, up to 30 fps (85,841 at 30 fps, rest 10 fps); plus 100k bbox-annotated frames
datasets.split: images 1 fps 128x256 for image LDM; 2 fps for key frames

models.name: Video LDM (driving)
models.architecture: LDM, U-Net (Dhariwal), f=8, z 16x32x4, channels 224, VQ autoencoder codebook 16384
models.init_from: own image LDM trained on RDS frames

models.name: Video LDM (Stable Diffusion text-to-video)
models.params: ~3.1B (autoencoder + diffusion), ~2.2B trained; temporal layers 649M (SD1.4)/656M (SD2.x); interpolation LDM 1,509M
models.init_from: Stable Diffusion 1.4, 2.0 or 2.1 (spatial layers first fine-tuned on WebVid frames)

other.upsampler: SD 4x latent upscaler, 473M backbone + 449M temporal params trained, 977M total
other.text_encoder: CLIP ViT-L/14 (SD1.4) / OpenCLIP ViT-H (SD2.x), not trained

training.objective: denoising score matching, v-prediction (driving) or epsilon (text-to-video), loss over temporal layers only (Eq 2); masked variants Eq 3, Eq 5
training.lr: 1e-4 for temporal layers and image LDM (driving); 1e-5 upsampler image DM; 4.0e-5/5.0e-5 autoencoder fine-tune; 1e-4 SD spatial fine-tune; 1e-6 DreamBooth
training.batch_size: per GPU, driving key-frame model 9 on 40 A100-40GB; text-to-video key-frame 2 on 8 A100-80GB; interpolation 3 on 256 A100-80GB; see Tables 6-8
training.steps: driving image LDM 73K; key frame temporal 146K; text-to-video interpolation 402K; decoder 41K/35K/78K; see Table 6/8
training.hardware: A100-40GB and A100-80GB, 8 to 256 GPUs depending on model

other.diffusion: 1000 steps, linear noise schedule, beta0 0.0015 betaT 0.0195 (driving)
other.alpha_merge: learned alpha in [0,1] per temporal layer, scalar for text-to-video
other.noise_aug_upsampler: t sampled 0..250 in training; 150 steps (driving) or 30 steps (text-to-video) perturbation at inference
other.dreambooth: 256 regularization images, 800 iterations, lr 1e-6, trains U-Net and CLIP text encoder, 8-23 images per subject

inference.samples: FVD: 2,048 videos of 16 frames at 30 fps (10k for SD2.1 UCF-101); FID: 10k frames (50k for mountain biking); IS 10k samples; CLIPSIM one random prompt per MSR-VTT example
inference.prompting: UCF-101 class names used directly as prompts

parameters.steps_eta_guidance: driving LDM 200 steps eta 1.0 scale 2.0; driving upsampler 50 steps eta 0.0 scale 2.0; text-to-video keyframes 50 steps eta 1.0 scale 8.0 (see Table 6 column order)
parameters.context_frames: 0, 1 or 2; one image frame first then two frames when extending

metrics.name: FVD
metrics.definition: I3D features, 2,048 generated vs reference videos (random 16-frame sequences)

metrics.name: IS
metrics.definition: video Inception score with C3D trained on UCF-101, 10k samples

metrics.name: CLIPSIM
metrics.definition: ViT-B/32 CLIP similarity averaged over 47,840 frames

metrics.name: Human preference
metrics.definition: MTurk pairwise realism, non-forced choice, 100 videos, 4 raters per pair

eval.protocol: Single runs, no seeds or significance tests stated; MTurk workers from English-speaking countries, $0.04 per question.

availability.data: WebVid-10M and Mountain Biking public; RDS in-house; project page https://research.nvidia.com/labs/toronto-ai/VideoLDM/

results.claim: Training temporal layers barely degrades image quality: FID 47.00 with alpha=1 vs 48.26 with learned temporal layers.
results.quote: With αϕ=1, we obtain 47.00 FID; with the learnt parameters, we get 48.26 FID.

results.claim: SD-based text-to-video LDM has about 3.1B parameters of which about 2.2B are trained; Imagen Video has 11.6B.
results.quote: Out of this, only around 2.2B parameters are actually trained.

results.claim: Videos of up to 5 minutes validated on driving data.
results.quote: We validated this for up to 5 minutes

limits: Authors state the models are not suitable for productization (training data internet-scraped, research-only sources).
Synthesized videos not yet indistinguishable from real; deceptive-realism risk noted.
Convolutional-in-time generation of long text-to-video is fragile; prediction models for text-to-video left to future work.
Quantitative text-to-video trails concurrent Make-A-Video on UCF-101 FVD and MSR-VTT CLIPSIM.
Spatial fine-tuning on WebVid slightly hurts image quality; FVD acknowledged unreliable.
RDS is in-house, so main results are not reproducible by outsiders; no seeds or optimizer stated.
